quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Riding directly alongside another vehicle is:

options.text: Good because it helps with drafting.
Good because other drivers can see you better.
Bad because you may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
Bad because the other vehicle may think you are racing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bad because you may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly alongside another vehicle is dangerous. You may be in the vehicle's blind spot, and the vehicle may block your way to escape from other hazards.

questions.question: Hearing protection is:

options.text: Not needed if you wear a helmet.
Not needed if you carry a passenger.

questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Hearing protection lets you stay safe from noise while still hearing horns and sirens.

questions.question: Under good conditions, keep a minimum following distance of:
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, keep at least two seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: When exiting a highway in a group, use which riding formation?
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is best for group riding on straightaways. Switch to single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Your lane position should not:

options.text: Keep you out of blind spots.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should keep you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should stop other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: Moose on the roadway are hard to see because:

options.text: Most riders are not looking for moose.
A moose's eyes are above headlight level, so headlights don't reflect in their eyes.
A moose blends in with the background.

questions.correctAnswerText: A moose's eyes are above headlight level, so headlights don't reflect in their eyes.
questions.explanation: Moose are hard to see because they have dark fur and their eyes are higher than vehicle headlights. Unlike other animals, a moose's eyes do not reflect headlight beams.

questions.question: Proper riding clothing offers all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Proper clothing protects you from injury in a crash. It also protects you from weather and other everyday discomforts while riding.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly while in a curve, you should:

options.text: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
Use both brakes hard while still leaning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
questions.explanation: If you must stop quickly in a curve, first straighten and square the handlebars, then stop. If you cannot straighten, apply the brakes smoothly, reduce your lean angle, then increase brake pressure as you slow down.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, it is usually best to:

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane is dangerous when wet. When it rains, ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is usually the best choice.

questions.question: When you must both brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both actions at the same time and press harder on the brakes.
Do both actions at the same time, but focus mainly on swerving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: You need good grip on the road to swerve safely. Do not brake and swerve at the same time. Instead, do one action first, then the other.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Keep your hands on the clutch and brake levers.
Put the motorcycle in neutral when slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands on the clutch and brake levers.
questions.explanation: When you approach a dangerous area like an intersection, rest your hands on the clutch and brake levers. This prepares you to react faster to any hazards.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should stay near the front, right behind the leader. This allows more experienced riders behind them to watch and help them.

questions.question: Riders wearing helmets are ________ more likely to survive a crash than those without helmets.
questions.explanation: A helmet makes you three times more likely to survive a crash. This is true at any speed.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
Near the back of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should stay near the front, right behind the leader. This way they do not have to rush to keep up. More experienced riders behind them can also watch and help them.

questions.question: What should you do with your headlight during the day?

options.text: Switch between high and low beam.

questions.explanation: Use your high beam during the day to help other drivers see you. Use high beam anytime you are not right behind or coming toward other vehicles.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Use the rear brake hard while slowly increasing front brake pressure.

questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: When should a passenger get on a motorcycle?

options.text: Only when sitting as far back as possible.

questions.explanation: A passenger should get on only after the engine starts and the transmission is in neutral. The passenger should sit as far forward as possible without blocking the rider's control. The passenger should hold the rider's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the dog to lose interest.
Ride slowly toward the dog, then speed up and pass it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slowly toward the dog, then speed up and pass it.
questions.explanation: If a dog is chasing you, downshift and ride slowly toward it. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: How should you apply the front brake?

options.text: Squeeze the lever firmly and smoothly with increasing pressure.
Grab the lever with only two fingers.
Push down on the brake lever with your foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the lever firmly and smoothly with increasing pressure.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the brake lever firmly with all four fingers. Apply more pressure gradually for smooth braking.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: Riders can use hand signals instead of or with turn signals. When the left arm is bent at the elbow and points upward, it means the rider will turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are usually rectangular with white background and black text or symbols. Riders must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Which vest or jacket color would best help you to be seen?
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing while riding to be more visible. Bright orange, yellow, red, or green colors work best. Avoid dark or dull colors.

questions.question: When you are being passed by another vehicle, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane for safety. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to move back into your lane unsafely.

questions.question: When riding at night you should:

options.text: Use the vehicle in front of you to help see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the vehicle in front of you to help see.
questions.explanation: To stay safe at night, reduce your speed and increase your distance from other vehicles. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Stay flexible with your lane position at night.
